clues: This town is the chief town of a shore district in Honduras. It is a port on the north coast, by the warm sea of the Caribbean.
Strong trade winds hit its north face from October to February and wring out harsh rain. It is one of the wettest towns in Central America.
This town was formally founded on 23 August 1877. Its folk still mark that late summer date as the true start of the town.
Each May, a famed street party here draws huge crowds from far and wide. It honors Isidore, a saint linked to those who work the land.
It bears two proud titles, Eco-Tourism Capital and Entertainment Capital of its land. The titles mark it as a hub for green trips and bright nights out.
